analysis.title: Weekly guidance from our Investment Strategy Committee (Investment Strategy, November 16, 2026)
key_insights: A proxy for the Global Market Portfolio (GMP) is estimated at $276 trillion as of 10/30/2026, nearly four times its value on 12/31/2006. From 2022 to 2026 equities grew from 47% to 52% of the GMP, fixed income fell from 41% to 35%, real assets rose from 6% to 8%, and alternatives stayed around 5% to 6%.

In four stress events (2008, 2011, 2018, 2022) equities lost relative weight in the GMP while other asset classes gained share. In 2008 equities fell from 55% to 39% and fixed income rose from 40% to 54%. In 2022 rising yields limited the diversification benefit of bonds, while alternatives rose from 5% to 6%.

WFII concludes that no single asset class has provided the same diversification benefit in every stress period. It recommends keeping strategic exposure across fixed income, real assets and alternatives alongside equities, and says moving to cash may miss gains in other asset groups during risk aversion and miss the equity rebound afterward.

Recent election results could lead to a more regulated and disciplined data-center development environment. WFII expects power availability, grid interconnection, costs, permitting and community requirements to change the pace and economics of the AI buildout, not its long-term direction. Funded and permitted projects are seen as better positioned than later-dated projects needing power or approvals.

WFII says a more measured AI buildout could extend the capital-spending cycle and raise the strategic value of operating and power-secured capacity. It cites Google's acquisition of Crusoe's pre-developed Wyoming site as an example of de-risked, power-secured capacity. Delays could defer cloud revenue and development costs.

Within AI infrastructure WFII continues to favor established hyperscalers for their access to capital and power, geographic flexibility, enterprise relationships and integrated cloud platforms. It would become less constructive if monetization slows, project delays become cancellations, or capital spending fails to generate adequate returns and free cash flow.

High-yield credit stress is concentrated in the weakest borrowers. Spreads on CCC-rated bonds have risen sharply while BB spreads have not increased significantly. BB bonds make up more than half of the Bloomberg U.S. Corporate High Yield Bond Index, and CCC and BB spreads usually rise together in broad stress, which has not happened this time.
WFII stays neutral on high yield and prefers investment-grade corporate and securitized bonds. Its tactical chart lists High Yield Taxable Fixed Income as Neutral.

WFII remains favorable on Industrial Metals, citing demand from the AI buildout, electrification and power generation, and mined copper supply lagging demand. An average mine takes roughly 17 years from exploration to production. It expects an uneven path higher in 2027.

Speculative copper positioning more than doubled from March 2024 to its peak on September 4, 2026, and has rolled over through October 30, 2026. WFII reads this as investors possibly starting to price more balanced risks. Higher interest rates, elevated energy costs and uncertainty over AI infrastructure spending are cited as downside risks to metals demand.

WFII expects interest rates may stay higher-for-longer with inflation above the Fed's 2% target. It names Fed Chair Warsh as reiterating the commitment to price stability, and says investor expectations have shifted from lower rates toward rates staying elevated or rising.

The distressed ratio (share of loans trading below 80% of par) has risen since mid-to-late 2025. WFII says stress could broaden among vulnerable borrowers if rates stay elevated, and remains favorable on Distressed Credit sub-strategies.

Tactical guidance (6-18 month horizon) places U.S. Small Cap Equities, Developed Market Ex-U.S. Equities and Emerging Market Equities in the lower categories and U.S. Large Cap Equities and U.S. Mid Cap Equities in the higher categories, per the report's table layout. Digital Assets, Private Real Estate, Commodities and Private Infrastructure appear in the Real Assets table.

sector_views.sector: Communication Services, Software and Information Technology
sector_views.rationale: AI adoption and monetization, earnings growth, competitive positioning and valuation remain the primary long-term drivers. AI investment in software is to be judged on adoption, monetization and customer returns.
Established hyperscalers are favored for access to capital and power, geographic flexibility and integrated cloud platforms, which matter more as capacity becomes harder to deliver.
Long-term demand from AI buildout, electrification and power generation outpaces mined copper supply, but elevated speculative positioning and near-term risks point to an uneven path in 2027.
Stress is concentrated in CCC-rated borrowers while BB spreads are contained. WFII prefers investment-grade corporate and securitized bonds.
Higher-for-longer rates and rising distressed ratios may create opportunities to provide capital to challenged businesses and support restructuring.

macro_indicators.reading: Peaked near 9% in mid-2022; remains above the Fed's 2% target
macro_indicators.interpretation: The final stretch toward 2% has proven harder, supporting WFII's view that rates may stay higher for longer.

macro_indicators.reading: Hikes from near zero to roughly 5% in the prior tightening cycle
macro_indicators.interpretation: Cited as the cause of the sharp decline in inflation after the 2022 peak.
Nearly four times the 12/31/2006 value, with equities at 52% of the total.

crypto_views: Digital Assets are listed in the Real Assets tactical guidance table. The report gives no separate commentary on them. Bitcoin and Ether market capitalization is used in the Real Assets share of the GMP calculation.

trade_ideas.description: Favor investment-grade corporate and securitized bonds over high yield, with high yield held at Neutral
trade_ideas.rationale: Stress is concentrated among the weakest borrowers and quality offers a stronger first line of defense.

trade_ideas.description: Favorable on Distressed Credit sub-strategies that provide capital to challenged businesses and support restructuring
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher-for-longer rates and weaker margins may broaden financial stress among vulnerable borrowers.

trade_ideas.description: Favorable on Industrial Metals, especially copper, with expectation of an uneven path higher in 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Long-term demand from AI, electrification and power generation outpaces constrained mined supply.
trade_ideas.risk: Speculative positioning is elevated and higher rates and energy costs could slow global demand.

trade_ideas.description: Favor established hyperscalers within AI infrastructure
trade_ideas.rationale: Access to capital and power, geographic flexibility and integrated cloud platforms become more valuable as capacity gets harder to deliver.
trade_ideas.risk: Monetization slows, project delays become cancellations, or capital spending fails to generate adequate returns and free cash flow.

risk_factors: AI project delays turning into cancellations, or capital spending failing to generate adequate returns and free cash flow.
Slower capacity deployment could defer cloud revenue and development costs.
Higher-for-longer interest rates straining leveraged and small- and mid-sized borrowers.
Weakening CCC-rated credit could broaden if rates stay elevated.
Elevated copper speculative positioning leaves prices exposed to disappointment.
Higher rates and elevated energy costs could slow the global economy and reduce industrial metals demand.
Uncertainty around the pace of AI infrastructure spending could temper demand for metals.

tension_points.bull_case: A more measured, disciplined buildout could extend the AI capital-spending cycle and raise the value of operating, power-secured capacity held by established hyperscalers.
tension_points.bear_case: Delays could defer cloud revenue and development costs, and speculation about future capacity is the principal risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Monetization slows, project delays become cancellations, or sustained capital spending fails to generate adequate returns and free cash flow.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand from AI buildout, electrification and power generation outpaces mined supply, which takes roughly 17 years to develop.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated speculative positioning, higher rates and energy costs, and uncertain AI spending could slow demand and leave copper exposed to disappointment.
